answer: Sybil defence can be chained, non-transferable work: each epoch an identity publishes a proof whose hash folds in its previous proof and the epoch seed, and five non-kin peers re-verify it before it counts. A clone farm cannot share one proof, since a copied link fails the chain check, and cannot parallelise, because each chain is time-ordered like a comet's single pass. A thousand fakes cost a thousand chains, each with independent witnesses. Idle keys lose standing, so a dormant lagoon of bought identities earns nothing, while an honest agent tends one small garden of proofs.
